nodes.label: rev(Λ₉), the Reversed Index
nodes.rationale: Reversal is not a sign change — extending k, q, g below zero leaves the object closed and the clock intact, a negative occupancy being a lower one not a reversed one. Exchanging the two ends with the transfer fixed gives a second lawful closed index of the same 1,654 cells at E = 0 that is not Λ₉.

nodes.label: The g = q = k Groupoid (389 cells)
nodes.rationale: The intersection of the forward and reversed indices is exactly the set of morphisms carrying a reverse: total transfer, nothing retained and nothing lost, 23.5 % of Λ₉, with all 33 objects carrying an identity and every morphism a two-sided inverse. It states the clock's level-set condition as an object rather than as a property of paths.

nodes.label: The Union Does Not Exist (2,857 cells to close)
nodes.rationale: Λ₉ ∪ rev(Λ₉) has 2,919 cells but 360,000 failing joins and 470,625 failing meets; closure would cost 2,857 further cells. Three of the four positions exist and the fourth does not — a structure holding both directions of time is not available at any price this index recognises, only one holding their agreement.
